## Which file do I need?

Cognitive Terrain runs in your web browser. Nothing to install.

| You want to… | Download |
|---|---|
| Play straight away on any computer | **cognitive-terrain-0.20.html**, then double-click it to open in your browser |
| Read the rules | **Cognitive-Terrain-Field-Manual-0.20.pdf** |
| Controls and rules on one sheet, two-sided, to keep by the keyboard | **Cognitive-Terrain-Quick-Reference-0.20.pdf** |
| Run it for a group, build campaigns, see why it works | **Cognitive-Terrain-Practitioners-Manual-0.20.pdf** |
| Hear each week read aloud (optional) | the **Immersive Briefings** voice pack, on its own release: **voice-emma-1** |

Two-player games work as long as both players use a 0.20 build (0.20.0, 0.20.1 and so on).

## What's new

- **A smarter Standard opponent, just as fair.** Red now guards the nodes you
  have framed, goes after the nodes you hold in its mind so they stop paying
  you, and saves its extra moves for crisis weeks. Campaigns are as evenly
  matched as before.
- **A new hardest level: Elite.** Red plays like a Veteran under four harder
  rules, set out on the start screen when you pick it:
  - **It learns your playbook.** Play the same attack card on it three weeks
    running and its people recognise the trick: the card pushes less until you
    rest it for a week. The card is marked RECOGNISED, and Their edge on you
    warns you a week ahead.
  - **Hidden defences.** You cannot see its Watch Teams and Prebunks, and its
    moves that set them show only as a hidden defence. Attack a covered node
    and the whole group appears on the map.
  - **Dug in.** A node it wins back from you is harder to push until you hold
    it again. A bunker icon marks it.
  - **Blowback.** Each of your attacks on it that fails gives it a point of
    budget.
  - Elite's rules never apply between two players.
- **Veteran and Elite play better.** Red now thinks about your likely answer
  before it moves, keeps its budget when no move is worth making in the run-up
  to a crisis, goes after the nodes that pay you, and leans on a second area
  early in each run-up so its real aim shows late. It still gets no extra
  budget and sees nothing you cannot.
- **An easier week in review.** The same move twice in a row on the same node
  now reads as one line (×2), each reason is given once, and every attack
  says why it hit hard or soft: a wide or poor spread, a good or weak area for
  the card, a framed or watched node, and so on.
- **Your result card opens flush under Their edge on you** on the left side
  panel (it moves up when you fold that panel), and Red's move cards stand
  beside the right side panel, so neither covers the panel you are reading.
- Recruit is unchanged.
- The Field Manual, Practitioner's Manual and Quick Reference cover the four
  difficulties and the dug-in symbol.
